summary: Latency regression (p95 +2–3x) after Optimize recommendation applied to routing config
description:
Issue summary
Customer reports a sudden latency regression for their Dedicated deployment in us-east starting ~09:42 PT after applying an Optimize recommendation from the Console. The change was intended to reduce cost via more aggressive continuous batching + cache settings.

Impact
- p95 latency increased from ~1.2s to ~2.9–3.4s on /v1/chat/completions (streaming and non-streaming).
- Elevated timeouts observed on client side (increased retries).
- Error rate stayed mostly flat (<0.5%), but tail latency and queueing increased.
- Customer reports production feature degradation and requests immediate rollback / mitigation.

Customer context
- Pinecone Analytics, Dedicated tenant, prod traffic (~180–260 RPS peak), mix of short prompts and occasional 8k context requests.
- Models impacted: primarily llama-3.1-70b-instruct (pinned), secondary qwen2.5-72b-instruct (fallback path).

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: pinecone-analytics-dedicated-use1
- Region: us-east
- Runtime: serving-runtime v2.31.4

What changed (customer report)
- Console -> Optimize -> “Apply recommended configuration” for route: /v1/chat/completions
- Recommendation summary shown to customer (per screenshot in attachment):
  - Increase max_batch_size from 8 -> 24
  - Enable continuous batching “aggressive” profile
  - Increase scheduler queue_delay_ms from 2 -> 8
  - Enable prefix caching for prompts > 256 tokens
  - Switch quant profile from fp16 -> int8 (weights only)

Expected
Latency should not regress materially. If it does, operator should be able to revert quickly to last-known-good.

Actual
Latency regressed and support/on-call had to perform a manual rollback by reconstructing the prior config from logs and Console history, which is error-prone and slow.

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) In staging with similar traffic mix, apply Optimize recommendation that changes batching profile and scheduler queue delay.
2) Run load with mixed prompt lengths including long-context outliers.
3) Observe queueing and p95/p99 latency spikes when long-context requests coincide with aggressive batching.

Initial investigation notes
- Correlation is strong with config apply event at 09:41:58 PT.
- Hypothesis: aggressive batching + increased queue delay caused higher queue time under mixed sequence lengths; long-context requests “hold” batch formation, increasing tail latency.
- Secondary hypothesis: int8 weights-only profile increased warmup time and reduced effective throughput until caches stabilized.

Artifacts / links
- Slack incident coordination (internal): sources/slack/incidents/thread-1731349988.json
- On-call thread (manual rollback attempt): sources/slack/eng-oncall/thread-1731351402.json
- Dashboard pointers (internal):
  - Dedicated Cluster Overview: Grafana > Dedicated > pinecone-analytics-dedicated-use1
  - Route latency: API Gateway > /v1/chat/completions > p95/p99
  - Scheduler queueing: Runtime > continuous-batching > queue_time_ms

Request from customer
- Immediate rollback to pre-change configuration.
- Confirmation of what changed and assurance that Optimize recommendations have safety checks.
- Ask: provide audit log / history and a single-click rollback mechanism for future changes (ties to SUP-2423).

Current workaround
- Manually re-apply prior config values (reconstructed from console activity logs + last applied config snapshot in config-service logs).
- Reduce max_batch_size and queue_delay_ms; disable aggressive batching profile.

Proposed follow-up
- Tie this incident to the Safe apply + rollback mechanism project (Linear PM-412) so customers can one-click rollback.
- Add preflight validation warnings for mixed sequence length workloads when increasing queue_delay_ms + max_batch_size.
- Add canary apply + metric gates (p95/p99, queue time) for Optimize-driven changes.

Applied changes:
- max_batch_size 24 -> 8
- queue_delay_ms 8 -> 2
- batching_profile aggressive -> balanced
Leaving prefix cache on for now to avoid thrash; quant profile revert pending warmup concerns.

2025-01-14 10:33 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE / On-call): Post-revert, queue_time_ms dropping within 3–5 minutes. p95 latency trending down from 3.2s -> 1.6s. Still elevated. Planning to also revert quant profile to previous fp16 to eliminate potential throughput variance.

2025-01-14 10:41 PT — Mateo Alvarez (Runtime): Agree revert quant profile as well. Weight-only int8 should be fine generally, but rollout + warmup can cause transient stalls depending on kernel selection and cache. Also check for KV cache invalidation behavior; some settings flips can cause churn.

2025-01-14 10:52 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE / On-call): Reverted quant profile to fp16. p95 now ~1.25–1.4s (back near baseline). Customer-facing impact stabilizing. Marking mitigation complete; will continue to monitor for 30m.

2025-01-14 11:05 PT — Kira Thompson (Support): Updated customer: we rolled back optimization settings; latency returning to baseline. Customer asks for detailed change history + audit record (who applied, what fields changed). Logging follow-up; linking to SUP-2423 for audit log deliverable.

2025-01-14 13:22 PT — Chloe Martin (Console Backend): Confirming the Optimize apply action currently logs an event but doesn’t persist an immutable config version for easy rollback. This incident is a strong data point for Safe apply + rollback mechanism (PM-412).

2025-01-15 09:10 PT — Kira Thompson (Support): Customer confirmed latency recovered and asked if we can prevent this class of recommendation from being “one-click apply” without safety checks. We agreed to treat Optimize apply like a deploy: preflight + diff + canary + rollback. Shared that this is in flight (Safe apply + rollback).

2025-01-16 16:40 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE / On-call): Closing notes: Root cause likely tail amplification from aggressive batching + increased queue delay under mixed sequence length distribution. Manual rollback was too slow/risky. Action items:
1) Add preflight warnings/guardrails when increasing max_batch_size and queue_delay_ms together for routes with high seq-len variance.
2) Ensure config changes are versioned with immutable history + one-click rollback.
3) Add canary apply w/ metric gates: p95 latency, queue_time_ms, timeout rate.
Linking to Linear PM-412 + upcoming rollback endpoint work.
resolution: Mitigated by manually reverting batching/scheduler knobs and reverting quantization profile to prior known-good values. Latency returned to baseline within ~20 minutes of the initial customer report. Follow-up work tracked for Safe apply + rollback mechanism (immutable version history, diff/preview, canary + metric gates, one-click rollback) and improved preflight guardrails for Optimize recommendations.
next_steps: Product/Eng: incorporate this incident into Safe apply + rollback requirements (diff/preview + rollback button) and prioritize Dedicated tenants.
SRE/Runtime: document recommended safe defaults for batching knob changes (queue_delay_ms, max_batch_size) for mixed seq-len workloads.
Console/Platform: ensure audit events include who/what/where + linked ticket, and expose config version history to support/enterprise admins.
